answer: activate is one operational-mode verb with several sub-parameters: activate swimage (activates the installable image; implies a system restart; db-action auto|empty-db|upgrade-db|rollback, default auto), activate database (activates the currently inactive database; restart-type cold|warm, default cold; sanity-check-override false/true, default false), activate activate-file, activate location-led (entity = chassis or card, led-mode flash|solid default flash, timeout 0..120 s default 0), activate loopback (WSS loopback on an NMC), activate eqpt-fw (resource plus fw-image-name), activate krp (installs a Key Replacement Package), activate otdr and activate otdr-fiber-check. For the database snapshot case there is a separate command: activate-snapshot db-instance <string> db-paraphrase <string> [sanity-check-override <true|false>], pre-condition being that a snapshot must already have been taken with take-snapshot.

capabilities is the per-card one: show capabilities-<name>, where name is the card name, available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. l0-capabilities is the photonic one: show l0-capabilities shows the capability details related to the node's Layer 0 functions; it takes no parameters. oadm-capabilities is the add/drop one: show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs], where max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees (20, uint8; 0 if not supported, and 0 by convention for ILA node-type which has only 2 fixed directions) and max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups (110, uint8; 0 if not supported). Degrees and ADGs are only supported on OADM node types.

Use show controller-card-<name> for just the controller: it reports redundancy-status (active, standby, not-in-service; default not-in-service), redundancy-standby-status (ready-synchronized, not-ready-synchronizing, not-ready-synchronize-fail, lock-out, card-not-present; default not-ready-synchronizing), number-of-switchover-events (uint32) and time-of-last-switchover (both visible only on the active controller), and additional-details (string 0..128). Use card (add/set/show/delete card-<name>) for any provisioned card in the shelf: required-type, required-subtype, card-mode, category, chassis-name, slot-name, power-profile, last-reboot-reason, admin-state and so on. Use show supported-card-<card-type> for what a model supports: category, card-width, card-height, max-power-draw, grid-mode-support, supported-card-mode, support-serdes-config, location-led-support, supported-bands, supported-features.

macsec-entity is the Ethernet MACsec one: add/set/show/delete macsec-entity-<name> with supporting-facility (an ethernet facility), enabled (default true), link-security-control must-secure|should-secure (default must-secure), replay-protection enable|disable, replay-protection-window 0..4294967295 (default 0), and a read-only negotiated-cipher-suite. secure-entity is the optical/L1 one: add secure-entity-<name> supporting-facility <value> remote-secure-entity <value>, where remote-secure-entity is the remote optical-carrier (G40), remote ODU (G30) or remote OTUFlex; enabled default false, re-key-frequency 3600..86400 s default 28800, re-key-fail-policy kill-traffic|continue-traffic default continue-traffic, traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 s default 0. Cipher terms live outside both: for MACsec in mka-policy (macsec-cipher-suite, confidentiality-offset), and for the optical side in secure-entity-sa-proposal, which shows encryption-algorithm aes-gcm-16, encryption-key-length key-length-256, integrity-algorithm none and dh-group ecp-521.

ase-idler-service is the Layer 0 service that fills unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum with ASE. It supports add/delete/set/show; ase-idler-enable is enabled|disabled (default disabled), ase-idler-state shows ase-enabled, ase-partially-enabled, ase-faulted or ase-disabled (default ase-disabled), function is idler, alarm-report-control allowed|inhibited default allowed. ase-idler-source is the physical ASE pump feeding it: set/show only, with pump-enable enabled|disabled (default disabled), pump-state, target-output-power range -3.00..20.50 dBm default 13, admin-state lock|unlock|maintenance default unlock, and function ase-idler-source. sw-service does not belong with them at all: it is a software command, show sw-service-<sv-name> / show sw-services, listing OS services and containers on the node with state off|ok|fail, cpu-usage, memory-usage, uptime, last-start-time and reboot-count.

No, they are not harmless. change-ztp-mode [-f] [ztp-mode=]<enabled|disabled> is an operational-mode command: change-ztp-mode enabled starts ZTP, reverts the database to the factory default and triggers a system reboot; change-ztp-mode disabled stops ZTP, including one already in progress. Use show ztp to read the current mode. clear [-f] recover-mode clears the recover-mode flag, confirming the current configuration as is, re-enabling communication with the line cards and potentially reconfiguring the traffic settings, so it may be traffic impacting; it takes no parameters and prompts for confirmation unless -f is given. The carrier-mode commands are the harmless ones: golden-carrier-mode, supported-carrier-mode and gcmt are all show-only retrieval commands for carrier-mode tables (capacity, client-mode, baud-rate, application, compatibility-id, status).

State: show third-party-app-<app-name> reports state running|stopped|failed (default stopped), plus version, vendor, product, label, information and enable (true/false, default false; when enabled the app is started and also restarts on system restart). show third-party-app-info-<location-id>/<app-name> gives per-location version, state and information. Firmware side: show third-party-fw-<fw-name> gives file-status valid|invalid|missing, path, version, crc, vendor, part-number, nsa-upgrade-version, present-in-eqpt and applicable-eqpt (max 80 elements each). Clearing: clear [-f] app [app-name=]<value> clears third-party apps. To control rather than clear one, use appctl [app-name=] [command=] with command restart, netls or exec, target defaulting to system, and up to 50 optional parameters.

Per-session is cli-session-config: set cli-session-config-<session-id> cli-lines <value> changes rows for that login only. cli-lines range is 10..1000, default 40; cli-columns 80..4000, default 80; interactive-mode true/false default true (set per session, not persistent); display-timestamp true/false default false. The protocol as a whole is cli: set/show cli with enabled (default true; CLI cannot be disabled from within a CLI session), port 1..65535 default 22, script-dir, default-interactive-mode (default true, affects only newly created sessions), and show-alarm-columns (default default-columns, global effect on all CLI sessions). The two system-configuration objects are config (show config [<entity-id>|<entity-type>], showing non-default configuration recursively from the current scope) and extended-config (add/delete/show extended-config-<name>, a non-standard global exception whose name must match one known by the system).

set is the generic attribute assignment: set [-f|-v] [<entity id>] <attribute> <value> ... [<filter> ...], valid in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, supporting wildcards (card-*, port-1-4-*), ranges card-1-[1..4] and lists interface-[DCN,CRAFT]; it asks for confirmation when the request may be traffic impacting or implicitly affects multiple instances. set-alarm-state is the alarm-state operation: set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>...), states none, ack and close, alarm-id-list taking 1 to 10 alarm ids, acknowledge-text a string 0..256. set-time is the time operation: set-time [new-time=]<value> in ISO 8601 form 2017-01-12T10:22:25Z or with +/-hh:mm, only applicable when time-source is manual (NTP not enabled). The one ending in -set is named-value-set: add/set/delete/show named-value-set-<db-entry-name>/<named-value-set-name> [value], value being a string 1..1024 characters.

mc is the Media Channel: add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value>, frequencies in MHz, with center-frequency and slot-width calculated by the system, and auto-delete disabled|enabled default disabled (only allowed on RD66TM sleds with l0-mode-op=hsc-ols). nmc is the Network Media Channel, the actual carrier-bearing channel: add nmc-<name> parent-facility <value> center-frequency <value>, where parent-facility can be an MC or an OMS, center-frequency 190650000..196700000 MHz, width 15000..200000 MHz default 35000, plus power and attenuation targets, ASE insertion and loopback state. The fillers are read-only occupancy reporting: mc-f (Media Channel Filler) shows lower-frequency, upper-frequency and slot-width only; nmc-f (Network Media Channel Filler) adds set of admin-state and alarm-report-control plus alloc-/actual- lower and upper frequency, alloc-bandwidth default 75000 MHz, actual-bandwidth default 0, and power-actual-tx/rx.

The scan is run by activate: activate otdr [entity=]<port> [[otdr-file-prefix=]<value>] triggers a measurement on an OTDR port, and activate otdr-fiber-check [entity=]<ots-r-id> triggers a manual OTDR-based fiber check (up to 3 OTDR tests; it errors if a manual scan or automatic Raman fiber check is already in progress). Tuning lives in otdr-ptp: otdr-range auto or 0..300.0 km, otdr-pulse-width auto or 10..20000 ns, otdr-measurement-speed fast|medium|slow|precision|auto|high-precision (default auto), otdr-ior auto or 1.0..2.0, otdr-fiber-type (default auto), otdr-resolution auto or 0.4..100.0, otdr-direction-mode default counter-prop-in-service, peak-power auto or 5..14.5, launching-fiber-length 0..50 m default 0. Results come out on otdr-ptp as otdr-fiber-break-distance (km, or not-available), otdr-last-measurement and otdr-last-measurement-file (.sor). Live status is on otdr: otdr-state not-available|idle|measuring|finished|fail, otdr-measurement-time, otdr-measurement-direction and otdr-error.

The name server entry comes back because of origin. dns-server-<address> has an origin attribute of dhcp (address assigned to this system by a DHCP server) or manual (default manual); a DHCP-learned entry is re-supplied unless you convert it by setting origin to manual. The global gate is dns assignment-method, which is manual, dhcp or both (default both), alongside enabled (default true) and search (a DNS search suffix that must contain at least one dot). For the relay, there are two levels: global dhcp-relay with mode disabled|ipv4|ipv6 (default disabled) and server-address (at least one IP must be configured when enabled), and per-interface if-dhcp-relay-<if-name> with dhcp-relay-enabled true/false, default false, which obeys the global dhcp-relay settings. A relay does nothing if either the global mode is disabled or the interface flag is left at false.

clear [-f] system [type=]<value> [[target=]<value>] [[restart-behavior=]<value>] does a secure wipe with three types. factory-reset resets the system or a particular equipment to factory configuration, stopping target traffic services and removing respective files and user configurations; it does not take effect for G30 Optical Carrier-Cards (OCC2T, OCC2E) but is supported on the G30 controller card (FRCU). full-wipe cleans the entire system and reinstalls SW on the controller and line cards, removing all files, configurations and software, and requires a base software reinstall from ONIE to recover. inactive just clears the inactive software partition. target may be the whole system (the default if omitted) or a chassis/card AID; restart-behavior is restart (default) or shutdown, and factory-reset with shutdown is not supported on L0 cards. The option that leaves logs and PM behind is clear [-f] database (clear-type full, keep-networking or initialize-from-script, default full): it sets the NE database to default and reboots, but explicitly does not wipe logs, PM data or other non-configuration data.

Read show unprovisioned-inventory-<chassis-serial-number>/<slot-name>: it lists inventory detected but not yet accepted by the Node Controller in a multi-chassis configuration, with hardware-version, actual-type, actual-subtype, sw-support-revision, PON, serial-number, clei, vendor, part-number, manufacture-date and detection-timestamp (the last time the Node Controller detected it). Anything appearing there has been seen but not taken in. Cross-check the cabling with show nct-connection-<src-port>/<dst-port>, which shows src-chassis, dst-chassis and src-/dst-chassis-state as node controller, provisioned or unprovisioned; unprovisioned ports appear in the form <chassis-serial-number>-<slot>-NCT-<id>. On the chassis object itself, show chassis-<name> reports is-node-controller, chassis-role (unknown, main-chassis, sub-chassis), expected-serial-number (which is how you tell the NC the serial number of a sub-chassis) and equipment-discovery-ready.

control-mode decides it: auto-max-pw (the default, auto mode targeting maximum output power) means the system sets the gain, manual means you set it. In manual mode gain-target applies, range 0..40 dB, default 0.0; in auto mode gain-adjustment applies as a user offset in the range -20.00..20.00 dB, default 0, and is only supported on amplifiers whose function is pa or inline. amp-control-support reports whether auto-max-pw is even configurable (auto vs manual-only). Setting control-mode to manual automatically sets gain-range-control to manual, and auto-max-pw sets it to auto. Things that stop output entirely: amplifier-enable disabled (the default) so no output power at all; forced-shutdown true on dual-band cards; admin-state lock; and for the underlying dependency, output power needs the OSC signal on an ILA node, or OMS facilities plus an OXcon on an OADM node. On input OLOS the amplifier shuts down after olos-shutdown-soak-timer (0..2000 ms, default 0) unless olos-shutdown-disable is true.

The live member is shown by protection-unit: show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> reports state (active, standby, available, unknown) and role (working or protection), plus transport-entity and AID. On the group, show protection-group-<name> pg-state gives the overall condition (no-request, forced-to-working, sf-on-working, wait-to-restore, unavailable and so on) and last-switch-trigger the reason for the last switchover. Behaviour is set on protection-group: protection-type y-cable or snc-n (default y-cable), switching-mode unidirectional or bidirectional (default unidirectional), reversion-mode revertive or non-revertive (default non-revertive), hold-off-timer 0..10000 ms in 1 ms steps (default 0), wtr-timer 60..720 s (default 300, revertive only) with remaining-wtr, pg-request (clear, manual-to-working/protection, forced-to-working/protection, protection-lockout, exercise), pg-control-request freeze/clear-freeze, and the trigger switches client-side-olos-trigger, client-side-sd-trigger, network-side-csf-trigger, network-side-sd-trigger (all default disabled). Manual switching is done with protection-switch operation-type force|lockout|manual|release.

Trigger the check with verify [-f] fiber-connection [target-select=]<port-id> [allow-switching]. If no port-id is given, all paths are verified; allow-switching is false by default, meaning only active paths are checked, and true lets the system initiate OPSM switching so both active and inactive paths are verified. The pre-condition is that equipment-policies cable-id-control is set to enabled; when accepted the system raises CID-verification-in-progress against the NE and replies that verification has started. Watch progress with show cable-id-status: cable-id-state is idle, running-incl-switching or running-no-switching, and test-progress is a string of the form 'N out of M completed'. Per-pair results are in show cable-id-path-<name>: port-a-to-port-z-last-test-status and port-z-to-port-a-last-test-status (not-verified, pass, fail), path-status enabled/disabled, last-test-qualifier up-to-date/out-dated, last-test-timestamp and additional-info (Cable-ID TxLOS, RxLOS, Cable-ID-MISMATCH, RxLOF, Power out-of-range, timeout). show -r adds the supporting fiber connections. terminate cable-id stops running tests.

Where authentication is sent is aaa-server: add/set aaa-server-<server-name> protocol-supported RADIUS|TACACSPLUS (default RADIUS), server-address, server-priority 1..10 (lower number is higher precedence; if omitted the new server gets the lowest precedence in use plus 1), server-port default 49, server-port-authentication default 1812, server-port-accounting default 1813, shared-secret (max 64 characters accepted, default sharedkey), source-ip (source IP used for RADIUS communications), role-supported authentication/authorization/accounting, and enabled default true. What happens when the box does not answer is governed by timeout, 1..90 seconds default 5, and retry, 0..5 default 1, with the total wait time timeout x (retry + 1) required to be under 5 minutes, plus security-policies aaa-authentication-method: local-only (the default), local-first-then-remote, remote-first-then-local, or remote-unavailable-then-local. Authorization fallback is set separately by security-policies aaa-authorization-method.

For the automation account use ssh-authorized-key: add ssh-authorized-key-<user-name>/<key-id> public-key <value> [label], one trusted public key per entry for SSHv2 user authentication; user-name may be a local or remote user, key-id is a string 1..64, public-key is up to 2048 characters in OpenSSH/PEM form, and public-key-algorithm is reported as ecdsa-sha2-nistp256/384/521 or ssh-rsa2048/3072/4096. Also set security-policies ssh-authentication-method to public-key or public-key-or-password (default is password). For the remote host the node copies files to, use ssh-known-host: add ssh-known-host-<id> address <value> public-key-algorithm <value> public-key <value>, where address is a hostname/IPv4/IPv6 and the algorithm may additionally be ssh-ed25519 (from R9.0); enforcement is by security-policies ssh-strict-host-key-checking, strict or relaxed (default relaxed). The node's own identity is ssh-host-key (show only, one per algorithm, with fingerprint md5 or sha256), generated or replaced by ssh-keygen [-b=<length>] [-l=<label>] [-t=<rsa|ecdsa|ed25519>], default type rsa.

The key agreement policy lives in mka-policy: add/set/show/delete mka-policy-<name> with key-server-priority (used by MKA to select the key server), macsec-cipher-suite for Secure Association Key derivation, confidentiality-offset (the number of octets in an Ethernet frame sent as unencrypted plain text), and sak-rekey-interval. Session key rollover is that sak-rekey-interval, in seconds, range 0 or 30..65535, default 30 s. The policy is bound to the port through macsec-mka-<name>, which carries mka-policy (the policy name to use), is-key-server (default false), connectivity-association-key and connectivity-association-key-name (strings 0..64), psk-lifetime in days range 1..173 default 14, psk-expiration-warning, psk-lifetime-enable and psk-configured-timestamp. Watch the channels with show sc-tx-<name>/<index> and show sc-rx-<name>/<index>: each gives sci-tx / sci-rx (16-character hex string), state in-use or not-in-use, association-number, key-identifier and next-packet-number. The port-level object is macsec-entity, which also reports negotiated-cipher-suite.

NETCONF listens on port 830 via ssh, enabled true by default (it cannot be disabled from within a NETCONF session), with hello-timeout 1..3600 seconds default 2, annotate-cli-name default false, and static-info-in-notifs up to 10 YANG identifiers. gNMI/gRPC listens on port 50051, enabled true by default, with gnmi-get-encoding-granularity per-path or per-object, default per-object; the grpc object is system managed and cannot be manually deleted. Nothing on those two is off out of the box. The one partly off by default is RESTCONF: enabled is true and https-enabled is true on port 8181, but http-enabled is false by default on port 8080, and RESTCONF HTTP access is not supported in secure mode. RESTCONF cookie-timeout is 1..300 minutes, default 5. All three port fields accept 1..65535.

restart [-h] [-f] [<resource-id>] [<type>] [<sub-component>] defaults to a warm restart if no type is given, and restarts the active node controller if no resource-id is given; it prompts for confirmation unless -f is used. warm reboots the processor of the card and is non-service affecting, with connectivity regained within five minutes (on XMM4 it is non-service affecting but visibility is lost for 3 minutes). cold reboots all components and sub-components and is service affecting, again with connectivity back within five minutes; cold reboot of XMM4 is not service affecting though visibility is lost, while cold reboot of CHM6, UCM4 and similar is service affecting. shutdown gracefully shuts the card down. No, you cannot assume uniformity: the guide states explicitly that not all cards support all restart types. Restartable entities are card (cold, warm, shutdown), card sub-component (cold, warm) and tom (cold only); list sub-components with show card resources.

Three things must be in place. First, a serdes-template per TOM part number: add serdes-template-<name> [tom-part-number <value>] [card-types-applicable <value>] [ports-applicable <value>], where tom-part-number is a string 1..16 and ports-applicable is 'all' (the default behaviour, all ports considered) or up to 20 port names. Second, the actual parameter values as serdes-template-entry-<serdes-template-name>/<serdes-template-entry-name> value <value>, for example RxAmplitude, RxEQ, TxEQ, RxPreCursor, TxEQAdaptive. Third, the global flag: set equipment-templates use-serdes-templates enabled, which defaults to disabled; application of serdes-templates depends on this flag being true. Templates then apply automatically to all line cards that support serdes when a TOM with that part-number is plugged in. Manual serdes configuration is still kept even where it deviates from the template; swapping in a TOM with a different part-number resets serdes and re-applies the new template. Enabling the flag does not retro-apply, so force re-application with apply-template serdes-template [applicable-tom=]<list>.

ots is the Optical Transport Section, the fibre span itself: fiber-type-tx/rx (default SSMF), fiber-length-tx/rx auto or 0..500.0 km, span-loss-transmit/receive 0..80 dB, span-loss-reference configured or measured (default measured), external-attenuation-tx/rx 0..30 dB, target-power-setting manual|auto|auto-plan (default auto), and laser-safety-mode OPLM or APSD. oms is the Optical Multiplex Section, the multiplexed spectrum on top of it: monitoring-mode (intrusive, non-intrusive, not-monitored, dge-fixed-attenuation, ila-with-equalization, integrated-equalization), grid-mode flexible (default) or fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif, fixed-50G-7100, fixed-150G-40ch, lower-frequency 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 MHz, and attenuation-control-mode-rx/tx. ops is the Optical Physical Section on add/drop and other ports: role tributary, multi-carrier, general-purpose (default), ase-input or active-multi-carrier, input-psd-profile -30..-6 dBm/12.5GHz default -6, port-expansion no or y-cable. osc carries the supervisory traffic: osc-mode OC3 (155 Mbit/s) or 1GE for HSC OLS, l0-comm-interface-type ipv4 or ipv6, osc-control auto (default) or manual, target-output-power -2.5..4.5 dBm, tx-power-adjustment -6..6 dB, voa-attenuation-target-rx 0..30 dB default 10, and lof-soak-timer short or long.

The behaviour is configured on trib-ptp with tributary-disable-action, which says what the NE does towards the client equipment connected over the TOM when a line-side failure is observed. The default is laser-shut-off, so by default the node turns the client laser off. The other permitted values are none, odu-ais, send-ais-1, send-gais, send-idles, send-lf, send-ms-ais, and send-nos (G30 only), which insert a replacement signal instead of shutting the laser. Timing is set by tributary-disable-holdoff-timer, uint16 range 0..10000 milliseconds, default 0 meaning holdoff disabled; it applies only when the TDA action is laser-shut-off, holding the optical signal as it is until the timer expires before turning the laser off. Related switches on the same object are near-end-tda (enabled/disabled, default disabled), tda-degrade-mode (enabled/disabled, default disabled, for BERSD-ODU triggering ALS) and forward-defect-trigger (true/false, default true), which decides whether a received client forward defect such as LF or ODU-AIS flows through to the line side or triggers an egress TDA action. Example: set trib-ptp-1-5-T2 tributary-disable-action laser-shut-off.
